docs.task: How the native agent loop handles a response that stops at the output limit: the continue prompt, the retry count, and the failure it ends with.

asks: The continue prompt the loop sends after an output-limit stop
The failure the loop ends with

data_flow.step: Each turn builds a ChatRequest with `max_tokens` set to the model's whole output limit: `ostra_core::pricing::max_output(model)` from models.dev, or DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT (32,000) when unlisted, clamped to u32::MAX.

The provider streams the response. Anthropic maps stop reasons `max_tokens` and `model_context_window_exceeded` to StopReason::MaxTokens; OpenAI maps an incomplete response with `max_output_tokens` to the same.
The loop records usage, saves non-blank text as `final_text`, records the assistant message and pushes it onto `messages`, and computes `has_tools` from `resp.tool_uses()`.
`match &resp.stop` reaches `StopReason::MaxTokens if !has_tools`. If `continues >= MAX_TOKEN_CONTINUES` (3), the run returns `self.fail("The model kept hitting its output limit without finishing.")`.

Otherwise `continues` is incremented, the user message "You reached the output limit. Continue from exactly where you stopped." is recorded to the transcript (host.record_message) and pushed, and the loop `continue`s to the next turn, which sends the whole conversation including the truncated assistant message and the prompt. A turn from the loop counts toward MAX_TURNS (400).

On the failure, Run::fail emits a Status delta with the message and returns ExecutionResult { status: Error, error: Some(message), submit: None, usage: total so far }. final_text is not set on this path, so the text of the truncated responses is not returned.

patterns.description: Inside the per-turn loop, after the assistant response is recorded and pushed onto `messages`, the loop matches `resp.stop`. A MaxTokens stop with no tool_use blocks either fails the run (counter at the cap) or increments `continues`, records and pushes a fixed user message, and starts the next turn. `continues` is declared once before the `for _ in 0..MAX_TURNS` loop and is never reset, so the cap of 3 is per execution, not per consecutive run of truncations. A MaxTokens stop that has tool calls does not enter this arm: it falls to `_ => {}` and the tools run.
patterns.name: Output-limit continue arm in the native loop

patterns.description: The same helper ends the run for refusal, model-call failure, and the turn ceiling. It emits ExecutionDelta::Status with the message, then returns ExecutionResult::error(message) with the accumulated usage.
patterns.name: Run::fail ends a run as an error and emits the message as a Status delta

document.problem: When a model response ends because it hit the output limit and contains no tool call, the native loop in crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs sends a fixed user message asking the model to continue, up to a fixed number of times per execution, and then ends the run as an error with a fixed message. The exact text, the count, and the conditions that trigger and count the retries are spread over a constant, one match arm, and the Run::fail helper.

submit.findings_summary: In crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs (line 630), a StopReason::MaxTokens response with no tool calls makes the loop push the user message "You reached the output limit. Continue from exactly where you stopped." and start another turn. This happens at most MAX_TOKEN_CONTINUES = 3 times per execution; the `continues` counter is never reset. On the fourth such stop, Run::fail ends the run as ExecutionStatus::Error with the message "The model kept hitting its output limit without finishing." It also emits that message as a Status delta. A MaxTokens stop that carries tool calls skips this arm and runs the tools. Anthropic's `max_tokens` and `model_context_window_exceeded` and OpenAI's `max_output_tokens` all map to MaxTokens. The docs page docs/internals/executors.md line 157 and the eval fixtures in tests/evals/coordination.toml state the count of 3, and no unit test covers the continue arm.
not_covered: How the engine and runner handle the resulting Error ExecutionResult (execution_failed gate and retry policy)
submit.scope_covered: How the native loop handles an output-limit stop (continue prompt, retry cap, terminal failure) in crates/ostra-exec-native and the provider stop-reason mapping; the engine's reaction to the error result and harness executors were left out.
